Cell metadata records parallel mode, actual parallel use, three rollout files, two spawned agents, 32/34 quality, and no timeout.
Completed official status records the parallel run command, multi-agent configuration, artifact file list, protocol validation, and 32 of 34 tests passed.
Official evaluation completed successfully but solution_passed is false with 32 passed, 2 failed, 34 total.
Final response says the package, adapters, config, hooks, pytest integration, install check, and local smoke tests were completed, but submit was unavailable.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main transport trajectory for the parallel run; semantic details are projected into the parent and child raw-agent sources.
Parent inspected upstream behavior, spawned upstream_api and toml_config, wrote most project files, patched install/config/runtime issues, waited on children, interrupted toml_config, and finalized.
upstream_api child inspected Pylama 8.4.1 sources and tests, then returned a long research handoff about API surfaces and behavioral expectations.
toml_config child built overlapping package/config files in the workspace, ran upstream tests, restored setup.cfg Pylama sections, attempted final checks, and was interrupted.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same empty-workspace Pylama project and official submit attempt.
Cell metadata records serial mode, no parallel uptake, one rollout file, zero subagents, 25/34 quality, and no timeout.
Completed official status records multi-agent disabled, the final artifact file list, serial control validation, and 25 of 34 tests passed.
Official evaluation completed successfully but solution_passed is false with 25 passed, 9 failed, 34 total.
Final response reports packaging, metadata, CLI, config, async, hooks, pytest integration, linter adapters, and local smoke checks, but no submit tool.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main transport trajectory for the serial run; semantic activity is projected into the single raw-agent source.
Single agent inspected dependencies/upstream package, wrote the package and linter adapters, iteratively patched config/path/install issues, ran local smoke tests, and finalized without subagents.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a full installable Pylama clone with exported API, config parsing, multiple linter adapters, formatting, file scanning, async execution, hooks, pytest support, and local verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept broad implementation ownership while spawning upstream_api for upstream behavior research and toml_config for config/TOML and overlapping package work, leaving file ownership informal.
parallel.implementation: The parent and toml_config both wrote substantial package files; the parent added the final linter set, rootdir/install fixes, setup.py cleanup, and final assertion checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Child side effects entered the shared final workspace, including config and support files, but setup.cfg changed hands repeatedly and the parent ultimately delivered the reduced configuration.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included compileall, import/API checks, TOML and INI config checks, direct linter smoke tests, editable install, CLI version, stdin behavior, hooks, and a final assertion script.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluation still failed 2 of 34 tests; toml_config never returned a final handoff because it was interrupted near closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same full Pylama project surface, including package metadata, exported APIs, config loaders, linter wrappers, async checks, hook support, pytest plugin, and support files.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned research, implementation, integration, testing, and final response, so there was no cross-agent file ownership or handoff boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote the package in large patches, added linter wrappers and support files, then patched TOML list handling, duplicate maps, path handling, install metadata, config discovery, select/noqa/modeline handling, and hooks.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All project files were integrated by the same actor; setup.cfg was added once as part of the initial package scaffold rather than being alternately restored and reduced by concurrent agents.
serial.verification: Serial verification covered compile/imports, config parsing, linter smoke checks, async/config/dedup, install metadata, CLI version, hooks, absolute paths, modelines, noqa, and missing-file behavior.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluation still failed 9 of 34 tests, indicating more hidden behavior gaps than the parallel attempt despite local checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the broad project requirements and explicitly built package, API exports, linters, config, scanning, hooks, pytest integration, async, and smoke verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad requirements and implemented the same general package surface in a single-agent workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No major requirement misunderstanding is visible; the difference is depth and completeness of behavior covered by the parallel implementation and local checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned upstream_api and toml_config while the parent continued implementing the same project in the root workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had multi-agent disabled and one agent owned the full workstream from research through final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained extra research and config/testing work but created overlapping file ownership; serial avoided coordination boundaries but had less total coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: upstream_api returned a large upstream/API summary, while toml_config worked directly in the same paths and observed parent-modified setup.cfg state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial transferred no context between agents; it accumulated upstream observations and applied them directly in its own implementation loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more context inflow but also stale/shared-state interface risk around which agent owned config files; serial had simpler but narrower context management.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote a broad package skeleton, then added linter adapters, fixed rootdir/config/install issues, and incorporated some child-created support files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a broad package in large patches and patched config, linter, path, duplicate, hook, and install defects found by local smoke tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation path produced a more complete official artifact, passing 32 tests; serial left more behavior gaps, passing 25 tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: upstream_api completed and its result reached the parent; toml_config remained active, timed out on waits, and was interrupted before a final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and closed after its own local checks and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unresolved child lifecycle, but the parent had already completed its own implementation and final checks; serial had no comparable join or cancellation risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents shared final implementation paths; setup.cfg was reduced by the parent, restored by toml_config, and then reduced again by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote setup.cfg once in its initial package scaffold and did not have another actor racing or overwriting config source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state overwrite episode; serial had no cross-agent write collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed broader local acceptance checks after edits, including compileall, editable install, CLI version, config/rootdir/TOML, stdin, hooks, and final assertions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also performed local checks but did not reach the same official coverage, and both runs lacked an exposed submit tool during the agent session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's verification loop was broader and more successful, reflected by 32/34 official tests versus serial's 25/34, though neither passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 214 LLM requests, two spawned agents, repeated waits, and an interrupt, but finished under budget after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 65 LLM requests, no child agents, and finished under budget after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more coordination budget and had a child still active at closure; serial was simpler but achieved lower official coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcomes are not discordant: both completed and both failed. The parallel run nevertheless passed 32/34 while serial passed 25/34. The process evidence supports a coverage difference: the parallel parent plus children did more upstream/test probing and broader verification, while serial implemented a comparable package alone but left more hidden-test gaps. The retained setup.cfg overwrite is a parallel-side adverse coordination episode, but it is not an outcome-differential failure because parallel scored higher.
parallel_contributors: Parent inspected upstream wheel/source and wrote a broad package plus linter adapters.
Child research and child config/test work increased available coverage and final artifact breadth.
Parent ran final compile, editable install, CLI, config, stdin, hook, and assertion checks.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership avoided coordination collisions but had less total investigation and hidden-behavior coverage.
Serial local tests caught many ordinary defects but official evaluation still found nine failures.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel fixed more modern dependency and packaging edge cases before closure.
Serial implemented many of the same surfaces but did not match enough hidden behavior to pass beyond 25/34.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both failed; supported comparative contributors to the score gap, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is present, but overwrite is more specific because the parent removed configuration source content that the child had restored.
